title: AI Note Taker for Sales Calls: How Lynkk Works, Before, During and After

lines: Every sales call ends the same way.
You write up the notes, pull out the next steps, send a recap, and try to book the next meeting before the deal goes quiet.
In this video, we'll show how Lynkk handles that work before the call, during it, and after it.
Lynkk is an AI meeting assistant.
It records your meetings and writes the notes.
It pulls out the tasks, with an owner and a due date for each one.
And it lets you ask questions across everything you've recorded.
There are four ways to record a meeting.
The Mac app records any call on your Mac, with no bot in the meeting.
The Chrome extension records a call in a Chrome tab, also with no bot.
The meeting bot joins Google Meet, Zoom and Teams links, or joins on its own from your calendar.
And for a meeting in person, you can record your microphone in the browser at lynkk.ai.
Let's follow one sales call, starting the morning before.
Connect Google Calendar, and on days you have meetings, Lynkk emails you a briefing.
For each meeting, it shows who you're meeting, your most recent note with them, and how many action items are still open between you.
So before the call, you already know where the deal stands.
When the call starts on your Mac, Lynkk notices it.
A card appears in the top right corner, with Record and Not now.
Click Record, and a slim column on the edge of your screen shows the clock, your audio levels, the live words, and a field for your own notes.
No bot joins the call.
Lynkk records both sides on two channels, so your side of the transcript is labelled You.
It's built for real calls.
On macOS 15.4 and later, Lynkk works to keep the card and the column out of your screen share.
Audio is written to disk from the first second, so bad Wi-Fi doesn't cost you the call.
And Lynkk stops on its own when the call ends, after five minutes of silence, or at the two hour cap.
After the call, you get the Meeting Brief, on every plan.
It has a title and a short abstract, key takeaways with timestamps, decisions with context, and open questions.
Every action item has an owner, a due date and a priority.
Click any timestamp, and the recording plays from that moment.
The transcript has speaker labels, in seventeen languages, four of them in beta.
On Pro, Summary Shapes rewrite the note for the kind of meeting it was.
There are nine built in, including Sales Call and Customer Interview, and every version is kept.
To follow up, the summary is emailed to you after every meeting, and to the attendees if you opt in.
You can also share a link you can revoke, or invite people by email.
Action items land on your tasks board, as a list or a kanban.
When a task belongs to another team, like a feature request from a prospect, send it to Jira from the note.
You pick the project and the issue type, and Lynkk creates one issue per action item.
It only happens when you click send.
Ask Lynkk, on Pro, is a chat that answers only from your own notes.
Ask what a prospect said about the security review, and the answer comes with citations.
Click one, and the recording plays from that moment.
Ask Lynkk can also take actions, each behind a confirm card.
Book the follow-up as a Google Calendar event with a Meet link, and it's done when you confirm.
For sales teams, a company workspace holds up to ten seats, and everyone in it gets Pro.
Each note is visible to admins by default, or Personal, so only you can open it.
Recordings are private to your account, and Lynkk never trains on your conversations.
That's a sales call with Lynkk: a briefing before it, a recording with no bot during it, and the brief, the tasks and the next meeting after it.
The free plan includes recording and transcription, the meeting bot, the Meeting Brief, tasks and sending to Jira.
Start free at lynkk.ai.
